get.summary: Whether YOUR telephony works, and why not
get.description: The one telephony read an ordinary agent can make about themselves. Every other route that could answer it is gated behind an administrator's permission, which is the wrong person: the user who needs to know why their Appeler button is missing is exactly the user who cannot look. telephonyEnabled is false when the institution has no ACTIVE telephony connection — which is most tenants, and the whole area should then be hidden. linkStatus is NotLinked, Active, Broken or Disabled: four values and not a boolean, because the repairs differ (nobody paired you, the provider stopped listing your account, an administrator unpaired you with a reason). canMakeCalls combines all three conditions — telephony on, you are paired, you hold Telephony.Call.Make — so a screen has one flag to read instead of three to recombine. A Broken link still allows calls; only Disabled stops them. Exposes nothing but your own state, so it needs no permission beyond being signed in.

post.summary: Pairs YOU with your provider account, found by your e-mail address
post.description: No body: the account is the provider account whose address belongs to exactly one CRM user, you. TELEPHONY_SELF_LINK_NO_MATCH when none does, TELEPHONY_SELF_LINK_AMBIGUOUS when two accounts or two users share it — an administrator then pairs by hand. 409 TELEPHONY_USER_LINK_ALREADY_TAKEN when the account is someone else's. Audited. Needs no permission beyond being signed in.

get.summary: The provider's user accounts, with the CRM account each one looks like
get.description: Reads the telephony provider's directory LIVE and proposes a pairing per account, matched on the e-mail address. A proposal is never applied: confirm it with POST telephony/user-links. An address several CRM accounts answer to yields no proposal and is listed in ambiguousEmails — picking one would be picking whose calls get attributed to whom. Already-linked accounts come back with linkedCrmUserId set. Answers 422 TELEPHONY_DISABLED when the tenant has no active telephony connection, 422 INTEGRATION_CAPABILITY_NOT_SUPPORTED when its provider publishes no directory, and 503 INTEGRATION_UNAVAILABLE when the provider could not be reached — the three are distinct repairs. Requires permission: Telephony.Settings.Manage.

get.summary: Which CRM users are linked to a provider account
get.description: Broken links first — those are the ones asking for action, and statusReason says what the nightly check found. Disabled links are excluded unless includeDisabled=true: they are history, kept because they explain calls already in the journal. Reads this module's own rows and never calls the provider, so it answers normally while the provider is down. Requires permission: Telephony.Settings.Manage.

post.summary: Confirm that a CRM user owns a provider account
post.description: Takes the pairing GET telephony/directory proposed, or one typed by hand. One CRM user holds at most one account and one account at most one CRM user: a live link on either side answers 409 TELEPHONY_USER_LINK_ALREADY_TAKEN rather than moving the account, because moving it silently re-attributes every call that follows. Confirming a link that already exists is a SUCCESS, and it revives one that was broken or unlinked. Audited. Requires permission: Telephony.Settings.Manage.

put.summary: The number this user's outbound calls present
put.description: E.164 only (a leading + and 8 to 15 digits): the value is handed to the provider's API verbatim, and a local form is refused there rather than here. A null or blank value CLEARS the override and falls the user back on the connection's default caller number, which is the ordinary state. Audited. Requires permission: Telephony.Settings.Manage.

post.summary: Switch a user's provider link off, with a reason
post.description: The link is DISABLED, never deleted: the agent's calls already in the journal point at it, and it is what explains why nothing new is attributed to them. The reason is mandatory and audited — an agent leaving, an account recycled and a mistaken pairing are three different facts. Unlinking an already unlinked link is a success. Linking the same pair again revives this row. Requires permission: Telephony.Settings.Manage.

post.summary: Ring my handset, then dial one of this record's numbers
post.description: Takes a RECORD and a SLOT — entityType (Lead | Customer), entityId, slot (Primary | Secondary) — and never a telephone number: the number is read on the server by the module that owns it, which also applies its own perimeter. An agency perimeter refusal therefore reads as the owning module's own code (CLIENT_NOT_FOUND, LEAD_NOT_YOURS). SYNCHRONOUS and never retried: the agent is waiting for their own telephone, and a retried call rings twice in somebody's hand — re-click instead. Answers 422 TELEPHONY_USER_NOT_LINKED when the caller has no active provider account (link one under telephony/user-links), 422 TELEPHONY_DISABLED without an active telephony connection, 422 UNKNOWN_SENSITIVE_FIELD or LEAD_PHONE_SLOT_EMPTY when the slot holds no number, 502 TELEPHONY_PROVIDER_REFUSED when the provider said no, and 503 TELEPHONY_NUMBER_UNAVAILABLE when the owning module could not be asked. The response carries the request id; follow it with GET telephony/calls/{callId}/context once the call exists. Audited. Requires permission: Telephony.Call.Make.

get.summary: Who is on this call, for the screen that opens while it rings
get.description: The other half of the screen pop: the realtime push carries a call id and nothing else, and this turns it into a name — under your permission and inside your agency perimeter, neither of which a websocket frame can apply. matchStatus says what to render: Matched is one candidate, Ambiguous is several (a family handset, a shop line — the agent chooses, with POST calls/{callId}/link), Unknown is nobody on file. A candidate with outOfPerimeter=true carries NO displayName: the caller is known to the institution elsewhere, which stops you searching for somebody you cannot see, and the record stays hidden. NO TELEPHONE NUMBER is ever returned. Requires permission: Telephony.Call.View.

post.summary: Say which record a call was about, or correct it
post.description: What makes an Ambiguous call useful: the journal refuses to guess between two people who share a number, and this is how the human who just spoke to one of them settles it. A manual attachment OVERRIDES an automatic one and is never overwritten by a later sweep. The reason is mandatory and is kept in the audit trail — a conversation filed against the wrong person is something a later reader must be able to understand. BOTH SIDES are authorized: only your own call — or one nobody is attributed, which is the agency's 'to attribute' queue — may be moved, and the target record must be one you may work (M01's agency perimeter for a client, M13's assignee-or-supervisor rule for a lead). A call that is not yours answers 404, because a 403 would confirm a colleague spoke to somebody; a record that is not yours answers 403 TELEPHONY_ENTITY_NOT_YOURS, because you can already see the call and 'not found' would send you looking for a record in front of you. Requires permission: Telephony.Call.Link.

get.summary: The call journal, filtered and paged
get.description: PERIMETER-FILTERED, and that is the point: you see your own calls, the ones nobody is attributed — the agency's 'to attribute' queue, which is the call most likely to be forgotten — and the calls of the agencies you cover. A tenant-wide account sees everything. The agency is the one the call belonged to AT THE TIME, so an agent moving branch does not take their history with them. queue=ToAttach|ToQualify|ToAssign are the three work piles, each a rule rather than a filter combination: ToAttach is anything not settled, ToQualify is ended-and-unqualified-and-not-dismissed, ToAssign is attributed to nobody. They compose with the other filters. entityType + entityId together give the calls of ONE record, which is what a lead's or a client's history asks for. canListen says whether YOU may hear the recording, so a screen does not have to probe for a 404. hasNote says a note exists and never what it says — notes are encrypted and never leave the module. NO TELEPHONE NUMBER is returned in any field. Newest first. 100 rows is the page ceiling. Requires permission: Telephony.Call.View.

post.summary: Say how the call went
post.description: The outcome must be an ACTIVE code of your tenant's referential — see GET telephony/call-outcomes — because two of its columns carry behaviour: one decides whether the call stops a lead's first-contact SLA, another makes callbackAt mandatory (422 TELEPHONY_CALLBACK_DATE_REQUIRED). A call that has not ended is refused (422 TELEPHONY_CALL_NOT_ENDED): the agent is still speaking. Only your own call — or one nobody is attributed — may be wrapped up; another agent's answers 404, because a 403 would confirm a colleague spoke to somebody. The note is kept ENCRYPTED and never leaves this module: it is excluded from the event M13 consumes and from every timeline summary. Wrapping up twice is allowed — an agent may correct an outcome — and M13 is idempotent on the call. keepRecording asks for the conversation to be kept, and is the ONLY way a recording is kept under the OnDemand policy. It is ignored under AllCalls (redundant) and under Disabled (it would be a way around the policy), and it cannot be un-asked by a second wrap-up. Audited. Requires permission: Telephony.Call.View.

get.summary: The calls nobody answered, grouped per caller
get.description: YOUR missed calls plus the ones attributed to nobody — the agency's 'to attribute' queue, which is the call most likely to be forgotten. A colleague's is theirs: showing it here would have two agents calling one person back. Grouped on a 30-minute gap between consecutive attempts, so somebody who tried three times in ten minutes is one entry with attemptCount=3 — and the callId is their LAST attempt, which carries the most recent reading of who they are. Calls already wrapped up are excluded, and so are the ones closed with POST calls/{callId}/dismiss. Voicemail counts as missed (somebody left a message); a FAILED call does not (an operator refusal has nobody waiting to be called back). No name and no number: read GET calls/{callId}/context for a name, which applies your perimeter. Defaults to the last 7 days. Requires permission: Telephony.Call.View.

post.summary: Close a missed call without calling back
post.description: Takes the entry out of GET telephony/calls/missed when no call back is needed. A reason is REQUIRED and is kept in the audit trail rather than on the call, because a column would hold the last reason only while a reviewer needs the sequence. Only a Missed or Voicemail call can be closed (422 TELEPHONY_CALL_NOT_MISSED): a conversation that took place has nothing to dismiss, and allowing it would be a way to clear a call out of a colleague's queue without qualifying it. Wrapping up is the OTHER way out of the list and means something different — it describes a conversation, creates a lead activity and may stop an SLA clock. Do not use an outcome code to mean 'nothing'. Your own call, or one nobody is attributed; a colleague's answers 404. Closing twice is a success. Audited. Requires permission: Telephony.Call.View.

post.summary: Turn a call from an unknown number into a lead
post.description: On your initiative, never automatic: most unanswered calls to a branch are not prospects, and a tenant whose every missed call became a lead would have a pipeline nobody trusts within a week. The lead gets a SYNTHETIC name ('Appel manqué du ...') because nobody spoke — replace it on your first real contact — and you become its owner. Idempotent on the NUMBER: a second call from the same caller answers the existing open lead instead of creating a duplicate. Answers 409 TELEPHONY_CALLER_IS_ALREADY_A_CLIENT when the number turns out to belong to a client (the call is attached to them instead), 409 TELEPHONY_CALL_ALREADY_ATTACHED when the journal already resolved the caller, and 422 TELEPHONY_NUMBER_UNAVAILABLE for a withheld caller id. Audited. Requires permission: Telephony.Call.Link.

get.summary: The tenant's call outcomes, in display order
get.description: What the wrap-up screen offers. Two of the fields carry BEHAVIOUR: countsAsContact decides whether the call stops a lead's first-contact SLA, and requiresCallbackDate makes callbackAt mandatory on the wrap-up. isSystem marks the platform baseline — renameable and deactivatable, never deletable, because a call wrapped up last year points at the code. Inactive ones are excluded unless includeInactive=true. Requires permission: Telephony.Call.View.

post.summary: Add an outcome of your own
post.description: The code is upper-cased and must be unique in your tenant — including against a DEACTIVATED one, which answers 409: re-adding a code somebody switched off is a reactivation (POST call-outcomes/{code}/activate), not a creation, and treating it as one would silently keep the old row's behaviour flags. Audited. Requires permission: Telephony.Settings.Manage.

put.summary: Rename an outcome and move it in the list
put.description: The LABEL and the ORDER only. The two behaviour flags are deliberately not editable: countsAsContact decides whether a call stops a lead's SLA, and flipping it would retroactively change what every call already wrapped up under that code meant — a month of SLA figures recomputed by a settings screen. To change behaviour, add an outcome and deactivate the old one, which leaves the history saying what it said. Audited. Requires permission: Telephony.Settings.Manage.

post.summary: Take an outcome out of the wrap-up list, or put it back
post.description: {state} is 'activate' or 'deactivate'. NEVER a delete, for a baseline outcome or any other: a call wrapped up last year points at the code, and removing it would leave that call explained by nothing. A deactivated outcome is refused by the wrap-up, so a screen holding a stale list cannot keep using it. Audited. Requires permission: Telephony.Settings.Manage.

get.summary: Whether this institution keeps call recordings, and under what basis
get.description: Disabled for a tenant that has never configured one, which is every tenant until a compliance officer decides otherwise — the feature ships built and switched OFF, because a recording is a person's voice and the lawful basis for keeping one differs by country and by what the customer was told before the tone. updatedBy is null when nobody has decided anything, which is a different thing from somebody having chosen Disabled. Requires permission: admin:compliance:manage.

put.summary: Decide whether and which calls are recorded
put.description: Any mode but Disabled REQUIRES a legal basis and a purpose: 422 TELEPHONY_RECORDING_LEGAL_BASIS_REQUIRED / TELEPHONY_RECORDING_PURPOSE_REQUIRED. They are free text in your own words — the bases differ by regulator and an enum would make the platform's list a constraint on what you may claim — and each is copied onto every recording at retrieval and FROZEN there, so shortening a retention never reaches back and lengthening one never extends a file already taken. Switching back to Disabled keeps the words, because the recordings already taken are still held under them. OnDemand keeps only the calls an agent asked to keep — the mode for a basis of consent, which is given per conversation. deleteAtProvider is honoured only where the provider supports deletion. Audited, payload included. Requires permission: admin:compliance:manage.

get.summary: Play a call's recording
get.description: Streams the decrypted audio and records WHO listened in tel_recording_access_log, in the SAME transaction — so there is no window in which a voice was heard without a trace. An authenticated stream and not a signed link, because a link only ever proves that it was ISSUED. Pass ?reason= when the caller stated one; it is optional here and mandatory on the export. 404 for a call with no recording, 422 TELEPHONY_RECORDING_NOT_AVAILABLE when the row exists but the bytes do not — pending retrieval, failed, or purged, which are different answers from 'never existed'. Requires permission: Telephony.Recording.Listen.

get.summary: Download a call's recording out of the platform
get.description: A different act from listening and a different permission: past this point no control of ours applies to the file. The reason is MANDATORY (422 TELEPHONY_RECORDING_EXPORT_REASON_REQUIRED) and is kept in tel_recording_access_log — it is the only thing that makes the export answerable afterwards. Served as an attachment. Requires permission: Telephony.Recording.Export.

post.summary: Freeze a recording against the retention purge, or release it
post.description: A hold suspends the RETENTION purge for a dispute. It is carried as a flag plus a reason rather than by pushing the retention date out, because the original date is the fact and the hold is the exception — merging them loses which was which. It does NOT survive an anonymisation of the client: a right-to-erasure request is a different instruction, and a hold placed years ago must not quietly veto one. The reason is mandatory when placing a hold. Audited. Requires permission: admin:compliance:manage.

get.summary: Call indicators by day, agent and agency
get.description: Read from a projection recomputed from the journal, not from the journal itself — so computedAt tells you how old the figures are. Internal calls (colleague to colleague) are excluded by design: counted in, an agent spending the morning consulting their manager would outrank one spending it on clients. Days are UTC days. Empty days are absent rather than zero-filled. crmUserId or agencyId null is the 'nobody' bucket — a call from a provider account no link resolves — and it is visible only to a caller who sees the whole tenant, because showing it inside one branch's figures would attribute another branch's work to it. Asking for an agency outside your perimeter answers an empty period, not a refusal. Defaults to the last 31 days; 400 is the ceiling. Requires permission: Telephony.Stats.View.

post.summary: Derive the indicators of a period again from the journal
post.description: Replaces every bucket of the period with figures counted from tel_call. Idempotent: running it twice gives the same rows, because nothing is incremented. Use it after correcting an outcome's 'counts as contact' flag, re-attributing calls, or restoring a backup — the nightly schedule only reaches back seven days. 400 days is the ceiling. Requires permission: Telephony.Settings.Manage.

post.summary: DEVELOPMENT ONLY — post a webhook to your own telephony connection
post.description: Signs the body you give with this connection's stored webhook secret and runs the real webhook's decision path: verification, deduplication, and the job that re-reads the call from the provider and journals it.
